statement_record.book: One-line gloss given while remarking that the proof of Theorem 5.5.9 generalizes: an elementary topos is a cartesian closed category with finite limits and a subobject classifier, a further generalization of the Grothendieck toposes of section E.4.

statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the three clauses of the book's gloss are the five fields: finite limits are carried by the standard generating data (terminal object + binary products + pullbacks), cartesian closure by [Closed] (imported from Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v at Structure/Topos.v:7, i.e. the LIVE cartesian-closed class, not the Structure/Closed.v Eilenberg-Kelly stub), and the classifier by [SubobjectClassifier]. Two presentational notes, neither a weakening of the definition: the library never DERIVES equalizers (hence 'all finite limits') from terminal+products+pullbacks — Structure/Topos.v's own header calls the pullback-from-equalizer reduction a known in-tree gap — and the class is genuinely inhabited (FinSet_Topos), with Pow 2 = 4 by eq_refl, so the definition is not vacuous.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition beck_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A) := {| quasi_inverse := Beck_Inverse; equivalence_counit := beck_equivalence_counit; equivalence_unit := beck_equivalence_unit |}   (* section binders: F : D ⟶ C, U : C ⟶ D, A : F ⊣ U, CR : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers U *)

Class CreatesUSplitCoequalizers (U : C ⟶ D) := { create_coeq {x y} (f g : x ~> y) (S : SplitCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g)) : ∃ (q : C) (e : y ~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e ∧ (∃ i : @Isomorphism D (U q) (scoeq_obj S), to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S); create_coeq_reflects ... : IsCoequalizer f g q e }

statement_record.book: Strict form of the monadicity theorem: for a right adjoint U : D → C, D is ISOMORPHIC (not merely equivalent) to the category of algebras for the induced monad if and only if U STRICTLY creates coequalizers of U-split pairs (Definition 5.4.8(c): every U-split coequalizer has a UNIQUE lift to a coequalizer upstairs).
statement_record.intree: Definition beck_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A), under CR : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers U; and Theorem monadic_creates : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers (EM_Forget T).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on exactly the point of the exercise. (a) Conclusion: an EQUIVALENCE of categories, never an isomorphism — the library's ≅[Cat] is itself equivalence-level (Instance/Cat.v:145 homset := Functor_Setoid, which identifies functors up to natural isomorphism; Theory/Equivalence.v:164 Equivalence_to_Cat_Iso converts an equivalence into a Cat-iso), and on-the-nose iso of categories exists only in Instance/StrictCat.v, which is never connected to monadicity. (b) Hypothesis: creation is rendered UP TO a packaged comparison isomorphism i : U q ≅ scoeq_obj S, not by a unique on-the-nose lift; Beck.v's header states the deviation outright — 'Mac Lane's strict definition demands a unique on-the-nose lift of the colimiting cocone ... the non-evil rendering asks instead that every iso-compatible lift be colimiting'. (c) The converse direction is proved only at U^T = EM_Forget; Beck.v:106-111 explicitly defers transporting it along K to an arbitrary monadic U.

gap: The strict version is absent in both directions. There is no 'strictly creates' predicate (grep -rni 'strictly creates|StrictlyCreates|strict creation' → 0 hits), no 'strictly monadic' notion (grep → 0 hits, though Riehl's own §5.3 names it), and no statement anywhere concluding an isomorphism of categories between the domain of a right adjoint and an Eilenberg-Moore category. What exists is the isomorphism-invariant analogue of both halves (beck_monadicity, monadic_creates); the exercise's content — replacing 'up to compatible iso' by 'unique on-the-nose lift' and 'equivalence' by 'isomorphism' — is entirely missing, and Beck.v documents the choice as deliberate.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition crude_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A) := {| quasi_inverse := Crude_Inverse; equivalence_counit := crude_equivalence_counit; equivalence_unit := crude_equivalence_unit |}   (* section binders, Crude.v:108-115: F : D ⟶ C, U : C ⟶ D, A : F ⊣ U, RC : HasReflexiveCoequalizers C, pres : PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers U, refl : ReflectsIsos U *)

statement_record.book: Exercise 5.5.iii asks for a proof of Proposition 5.5.8, the reflexive tripleability theorem: if U : D → C has a left adjoint, D has coequalizers of reflexive pairs, U preserves coequalizers of reflexive pairs, and U reflects isomorphisms, then U is monadic.
statement_record.intree: Definition crude_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A), given A : F ⊣ U, RC : HasReflexiveCoequalizers C, pres : PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers U, refl : ReflectsIsos U (with PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers U := ∀ x y (f g : x ~> y), ReflexivePair f g → ∀ q e, IsCoequalizer f g q e → IsCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g) (U q) (fmap[U] e), Crude.v:100).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the three hypotheses match one-for-one (the library names the domain of U 'C', Riehl names it 'D'), and the conclusion 'the Eilenberg-Moore comparison EM_Comparison A is an equivalence' is precisely Riehl's Definition 5.3.1 of monadic (Monad/Comparison.v:273 Definition Monadic U := ∃ F (A : F ⊣ U), EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A)). One presentational difference, flagged in Crude.v's header: hypothesis (ii) is stated elementarily on forks rather than through the PreservesColimit vocabulary — that is the standard crude hypothesis and is if anything the form the proof consumes. Note also that the in-tree dependency runs opposite to the exercise's hint: Beck.v (Theorem 5.5.1) is built ON TOP of the crude architecture rather than the reflexive theorem being adapted from Beck's proof, so the exercise's content is proved, by a different route.

evidence.intree_statement: Class LawvereTheory : Type := { law_cat : Category; law_terminal : @Terminal law_cat; law_cartesian : @Cartesian law_cat; law_of_nat : nat → law_cat; law_zero_terminal : law_of_nat 0%nat = @terminal_obj law_cat law_terminal; law_plus_product : ∀ m n : nat, (@product_obj law_cat law_cartesian (law_of_nat m) (law_of_nat n)) = law_of_nat (m + n)%nat }

Record Model := { model_fun : @law_cat T ⟶ C; model_cartesian : @CartesianFunctor (@law_cat T) C model_fun (@law_cartesian T) _; model_terminal : @TerminalFunctor (@law_cat T) C model_fun (@law_terminal T) _ }

Definition Models_Full : Construction.Subcategory.Full (@Fun (@law_cat T) C) Models_sub := fun _ _ _ _ _ => I   (* every natural transformation between the underlying functors of two models is a morphism of models *)

Theorem law_pow_one (n : nat) : law_pow n = law_of_nat n   (* with law_pow 0 := terminal_obj and law_pow (S k) := product_obj (law_of_nat 1) (law_pow k): every named object IS the n-fold power of the generic object 1 *)

statement_record.book: Prose definition interleaved in Exercise 5.5.vii: when the monad T on Set is finitary, the identity-on-objects I : N^op → L built from its Kleisli category is the ASSOCIATED LAWVERE THEORY; the objects of L are all iterated finite products of the object 1, so the essential data is the family of hom-sets L(n,1) of n-ary operations. A model of the Lawvere theory in Set is a finite-product-preserving functor L → Set, and a morphism of models is a natural transformation; the category of T-algebras can be recovered from this data [Lin66].
statement_record.intree: Class LawvereTheory := { law_cat; law_terminal; law_cartesian; law_of_nat : nat → law_cat; law_zero_terminal; law_plus_product } with Theorem law_pow_one (n : nat) : law_pow n = law_of_nat n; Record Model := { model_fun : law_cat T ⟶ C; model_cartesian : CartesianFunctor …; model_terminal : TerminalFunctor … }; Definition Models := Sub (Fun (law_cat T) C) Models_sub with Models_Full.
statement_record.strength_comparison: Mixed. The MODEL half is faithful and in fact more general than the book's: a model is exactly a finite-product-preserving (cartesian + terminal) functor out of the theory, morphisms of models are ALL natural transformations (Models_Full), and the target is any cartesian C rather than only Set (Riehl's Set case is Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v, with ev1 : Models T Sets ⟶ Sets). The THEORY half is intree-weaker in two ways: (a) it is a standalone class, not the theory ASSOCIATED TO A MONAD; (b) law_of_nat is only a naming function with propositional strictness equalities — bijectivity onto the objects is deliberately NOT required, so 'the objects of L are the iterated products of 1' is asserted only through law_pow_one for the named objects, and consumers must add reachability by hand (Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v's ev1_Faithful carries an explicit reachability hypothesis, witnessed on the base by FinSetOp_reach).
